description:
Access Graph (Identity Security) view — users, roles, resources, and security alerts backed by live SQL against the CNPG Postgres database.

IMPORTANT — two structural limits of the Access Graph apply throughout, and each affected panel repeats them in its own description:
1. Roles granted to SSO users by LOGIN RULES create no graph edge, so per-user role counts and "unused role" style panels under-report those grants.
2. Access Graph stores duplicate node rows for some roles, actions and resource groups, so counts use DISTINCT names rather than row or node-id counts.

panels.description:
Human (interactive) Teleport users. Machine identities are counted separately in *Bots / Service Identities*.

**Caveat:** the non-human split is heuristic — Access Graph carries no is_bot flag, so identities are classed as non-human by the `@`/`bot-` naming convention Teleport uses for generated identities. `localtest` is a leftover local test account and is counted as human because nothing in the graph marks it otherwise.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE '@%'
  AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE '@%'
  AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'

panels.title: Human Users

panels.description:
Non-human Teleport identities — machine/bot accounts and Teleport-generated internal identities.

**Heuristic:** Access Graph exposes no is_bot flag, so this matches the `@`/`bot-` naming convention Teleport uses for generated identities. A human account named outside that convention that is really a service account will be miscounted as human.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND (value->>'name' LIKE '@%' OR value->>'name' LIKE 'bot-%')
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND (value->>'name' LIKE '@%' OR value->>'name' LIKE 'bot-%')

panels.title: Bots / Service Identities

panels.description:
Roles authored by this cluster's operators (Terraform / tctl), excluding Teleport's own preset and system roles and the auto-generated `bot-*` roles.

**Counting note:** Access Graph stores duplicate node rows for some roles (32 rows for 31 distinct role names), so this counts DISTINCT names rather than rows. The previous query counted rows over all roles and read 32.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(DISTINCT value->>'name') FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
  AND coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(DISTINCT value->>'name') FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
  AND coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'

panels.title: Operator-Created Roles

panels.description:
Roles Teleport ships or generates itself: `preset` roles, `system` roles, and the `bot-*` roles created per machine-ID bot. Shown alongside *Operator-Created Roles* so the split is explicit rather than folded into one total.

Counts DISTINCT names — Access Graph holds duplicate node rows for some roles.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(DISTINCT value->>'name') FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
  AND (coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','')
       IN ('preset','system')
       OR value->>'name' LIKE 'bot-%')
```

WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
  AND (coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','')

panels.title: Resources

panels.description:
Security alerts raised by Teleport Identity Security that have not been resolved, dismissed or closed. Any value above 0 warrants investigation.

**Schema note:** this Access Graph build uses status values `in_progress` / `resolved`; the string `OPEN` never occurs. The previous query filtered `status='OPEN'` and therefore always read 0 while 22 high-severity alerts were live. This panel now matches on *not-closed* instead of guessing the open label.

**These alerts are raised by Teleport Identity Security itself and are triaged and actioned inside Teleport (Identity Security -> Security Alerts), not in Grafana.** This panel is the signal to go do that.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM security_alerts
WHERE lower(status) NOT IN ('resolved','dismissed','closed')
```
panels.title: Active Security Alerts

panels.description:
Users with a standing_privileges score > 0. Standing access is always-on access that does not require an access request.

**Caveat:** roles granted to SSO users via login rules produce no Access Graph edge, so SSO users' standing privileges are under-counted here (see *Users — Standing Privileges & MFA*).

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND (value->'properties'->>'standing_privileges')::int > 0
```

  AND (value->'properties'->>'standing_privileges')::int > 0

panels.title: Users w/ Standing Privileges

panels.description:
Users with at least one MFA device registered **in Teleport** (weakest_mfa_device_kind is set to a real device kind, e.g. TOTP or WEBAUTHN).

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND value->'properties'->>'weakest_mfa_device_kind' NOT IN ('UNSET','')
```

targets.rawSql:

panels.title: Users w/ an MFA Device

panels.description:
Users whose `weakest_mfa_device_kind` is explicitly `UNSET` or empty — Access Graph knows about them and knows they have **no** MFA device registered in Teleport. This is the only one of the three MFA states that is genuinely a finding.

Split out from a former single "Users w/o MFA" stat, which conflated *known absent* with *unknown* (property missing).

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND value->'properties'->>'weakest_mfa_device_kind' IN ('UNSET','')
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND value->'properties'->>'weakest_mfa_device_kind' IN ('UNSET','')

panels.title: Users w/o an MFA Device

panels.description:
Users for whom Access Graph carries **no** `weakest_mfa_device_kind` property at all — absence of data, not absence of MFA. Neutral by design, never red.

On this cluster this is `jturner@b1tsized.tech`, an SSO (Google OIDC) user. SSO users authenticate their second factor at the identity provider and legitimately have no Teleport-registered MFA device; counting them as "no MFA" would be wrong. Verify their posture in the IdP, not here.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND NOT (value->'properties' ? 'weakest_mfa_device_kind')
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM nodes
WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
  AND NOT (value->'properties' ? 'weakest_mfa_device_kind')

panels.title: Users w/ MFA Status Unknown

panels.description:
Operator-authored roles for which the Access Graph shows **no** member_of, impersonator_of or requester_of edge — i.e. no grant path the graph can see.

**Read this as a review prompt, not a delete list.** The Access Graph does not model login-rule / SSO role grants: a role handed to an SSO user by a login rule produces no graph edge at all. Verified on this cluster — `jturner@b1tsized.tech` has zero member_of edges, yet audit `access_request.create` events record their standing `user_roles` as `["role-base","role-grafana-access","role-kube-access-auto-approved"]`. All three roles currently listed here are exactly those, so all three are false positives. A listed role may well be live; confirm against login rules and the audit log before removing anything.

Teleport preset/system and generated `bot-*` roles are excluded — they are shipped unused by design and previously made up 14 of the 17 reported "dead" roles.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT r.value->>'name' FROM nodes r
  WHERE r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
    AND coalesce(r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
    AND r.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM nodes r2
      JOIN edges e ON e.to_node = r2.id
      WHERE r2.kind='identity_group' AND r2.subkind='role'
        AND r2.value->>'name' = r.value->>'name'
        AND e.kind IN ('member_of','impersonator_of','requester_of')
    )
) sub
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(*) FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT r.value->>'name' FROM nodes r
  WHERE r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
    AND coalesce(r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
    AND r.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM nodes r2
      JOIN edges e ON e.to_node = r2.id
      WHERE r2.kind='identity_group' AND r2.subkind='role'
        AND r2.value->>'name' = r.value->>'name'
        AND e.kind IN ('member_of','impersonator_of','requester_of')
    )
) sub

Bot identities that hold impersonation rights over at least one Teleport role.

**SQL:**
```sql

```

panels.title: Bots w/ Impersonation Rights

panels.description:
All users with their standing privilege score, role count and weakest registered MFA device kind.

**Caveat — roles_count under-reports SSO users.** It is derived from Access Graph `member_of` edges, and login-rule/SSO role grants create no edge. Verified: `jturner@b1tsized.tech` shows `roles_count = 0`, but audit `access_request.create` events record three standing roles (`role-base`, `role-grafana-access`, `role-kube-access-auto-approved`). Treat 0 for an SSO user as "unknown", not "none".

`mfa` reads `(unknown)` when the property is absent entirely — this is what an SSO user with no Teleport-registered device looks like; their second factor is enforced at the IdP.

The `crown_jewel` and `locked` columns were removed: both are `false` for every user on this cluster and carried no signal.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT
  value->>'name'                                  AS "user",
  value->'properties'->>'standing_privileges'     AS standing,
  value->'properties'->>'identity_groups'         AS roles_count,
  coalesce(value->'properties'->>'weakest_mfa_device_kind','(unknown)') AS mfa
FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
ORDER BY (value->'properties'->>'standing_privileges')::int DESC, "user"
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT
  value->>'name'                                  AS "user",
  value->'properties'->>'standing_privileges'     AS standing,
  value->'properties'->>'identity_groups'         AS roles_count,
  coalesce(value->'properties'->>'weakest_mfa_device_kind','(unknown)') AS mfa
FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity' AND subkind='user'
ORDER BY (value->'properties'->>'standing_privileges')::int DESC, "user"

panels.title: Users — Standing Privileges & MFA

panels.description:
Every user's direct SSH logins through their standing role memberships — who can SSH where, and as which UNIX user, without needing an access request.

**Deduplication:** Access Graph stores duplicate `action` rows per role (8 rows for 7 distinct ssh actions) and only one copy carries the logins list. The previous query joined row-by-row, so `olu` showed `logins = NULL` while `admin` showed `["root","ubuntu"]` for the *same* role. Logins are now unioned across every duplicate row for the role name; both users correctly read `root, ubuntu`.

**Known gaps:** (a) `jturner@b1tsized.tech` does not appear — their roles come from an SSO login rule, which produces no `member_of` edge. (b) `role-ssh-root-access` never appears because nobody holds it as a standing role; it is request-only (see *Access Request Escalation Paths*).

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
WITH role_logins AS (
  SELECT a.value->>'name' AS role_name,
         string_agg(DISTINCT l.v, ', ' ORDER BY l.v) AS logins
  FROM nodes a
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements_text(
    coalesce(a.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'ssh'->'logins'->'original_values','[]'::jsonb)
  ) AS l(v)
  WHERE a.kind='action' AND a.subkind='ssh'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  u.value->>'name' AS "user",
  r.value->>'name' AS role,
  coalesce(rl.logins,'(no logins listed)') AS logins
FROM edges m
JOIN nodes u ON u.id=m.from_node AND u.kind='identity' AND u.subkind='user'
JOIN nodes r ON r.id=m.to_node   AND r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
JOIN edges ra ON ra.from_node=r.id AND ra.kind='access'
JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=ra.to_node   AND a.kind='action' AND a.subkind='ssh'
LEFT JOIN role_logins rl ON rl.role_name = r.value->>'name'
WHERE m.kind='member_of'
ORDER BY "user", role
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
WITH role_logins AS (
  SELECT a.value->>'name' AS role_name,
         string_agg(DISTINCT l.v, ', ' ORDER BY l.v) AS logins
  FROM nodes a
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements_text(
    coalesce(a.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'ssh'->'logins'->'original_values','[]'::jsonb)
  ) AS l(v)
  WHERE a.kind='action' AND a.subkind='ssh'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  u.value->>'name' AS "user",
  r.value->>'name' AS role,
  coalesce(rl.logins,'(no logins listed)') AS logins
FROM edges m
JOIN nodes u ON u.id=m.from_node AND u.kind='identity' AND u.subkind='user'
JOIN nodes r ON r.id=m.to_node   AND r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
JOIN edges ra ON ra.from_node=r.id AND ra.kind='access'
JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=ra.to_node   AND a.kind='action' AND a.subkind='ssh'
LEFT JOIN role_logins rl ON rl.role_name = r.value->>'name'
WHERE m.kind='member_of'
ORDER BY "user", role

panels.title: Standing SSH Access

panels.description:
Bot identities and the Teleport roles they can impersonate. Bot impersonation grants the full permission set of the target role to the machine identity.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT u.value->>'name' AS bot, r.value->>'name' AS impersonates_role
FROM edges e
JOIN nodes u ON u.id=e.from_node
JOIN nodes r ON r.id=e.to_node
WHERE e.kind='impersonator_of'
ORDER BY bot, impersonates_role
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT u.value->>'name' AS bot, r.value->>'name' AS impersonates_role
FROM edges e
JOIN nodes u ON u.id=e.from_node
JOIN nodes r ON r.id=e.to_node
WHERE e.kind='impersonator_of'
ORDER BY bot, impersonates_role

panels.title: Bot Impersonations

panels.description:
Which roles can submit access requests, and for what. Maps the JIT escalation topology.

**Two different things, now in two columns.** A `requester_of` edge points at either another role (a role escalation) or a resource_group (a label selector bounding which resources may be requested). The previous single `can_request` column mixed them, so `role-base -> {"*":"*"}` read as "role-base can request any role" when it actually means "role-base may request resources matching any label". `can_request_role` is a real privilege escalation target; `can_request_resource_scope` is a search-as-roles resource filter.

The hardcoded `NOT IN ('requester','okta-requester')` blocklist was replaced with the preset/system label filter, so new Teleport presets are excluded automatically rather than needing the list updated.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT DISTINCT
  r.value->>'name' AS base_role,
  CASE WHEN t.kind='identity_group' THEN t.value->>'name' END AS can_request_role,
  CASE WHEN t.kind='resource_group' THEN t.value->>'name' END AS can_request_resource_scope
FROM nodes r
JOIN edges ea ON ea.from_node=r.id AND ea.kind='access'
JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=ea.to_node   AND a.kind='action' AND a.subkind='can_request'
JOIN edges e  ON e.from_node=a.id  AND e.kind='requester_of'
JOIN nodes t  ON t.id=e.to_node
WHERE r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
  AND coalesce(r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND r.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
ORDER BY base_role, can_request_role NULLS LAST, can_request_resource_scope NULLS LAST
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT DISTINCT
  r.value->>'name' AS base_role,
  CASE WHEN t.kind='identity_group' THEN t.value->>'name' END AS can_request_role,
  CASE WHEN t.kind='resource_group' THEN t.value->>'name' END AS can_request_resource_scope
FROM nodes r
JOIN edges ea ON ea.from_node=r.id AND ea.kind='access'
JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=ea.to_node   AND a.kind='action' AND a.subkind='can_request'
JOIN edges e  ON e.from_node=a.id  AND e.kind='requester_of'
JOIN nodes t  ON t.id=e.to_node
WHERE r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
  AND coalesce(r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND r.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
ORDER BY base_role, can_request_role NULLS LAST, can_request_resource_scope NULLS LAST

panels.title: Access Request Escalation Paths

panels.description:
For each operator-authored role, the reviewer roles that can approve requests for it.

**`wildcard_reviewer = true` means the reviewer can approve *every* role in the cluster**, not just this one — it is a blanket grant, not a targeted one. On this cluster every row is `true` because a single system reviewer, `@teleport-access-approver`, holds 36 `reviewer_of` edges covering all 31 roles. That is one identity able to approve anything, which the previous flat `reviewers` column made look like ordinary per-role coverage.

The `LIKE 'role-%'` name filter was replaced with the preset/system label filter; it was silently dropping the operator roles `admin-admin` and `ci-bot-role`.

**Limitation:** the Access Graph does not record access_request *auto-approval*. A role approved automatically by the approval bot and a role requiring a human reviewer look identical here. Use the audit log (`access_request.review`) to tell them apart.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
WITH roles AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT value->>'name' AS name
  FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
), rv AS (
  SELECT a.value->>'name' AS reviewer, r2.value->>'name' AS target
  FROM edges e
  JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=e.from_node AND a.kind='action' AND a.subkind='can_review'
  JOIN nodes r2 ON r2.id=e.to_node  AND r2.kind='identity_group' AND r2.subkind='role'
  WHERE e.kind='reviewer_of'
), wildcard AS (
  SELECT reviewer FROM rv
  GROUP BY reviewer
  HAVING count(DISTINCT target) >= (SELECT count(*) FROM roles)
)
SELECT rv.target AS target_role,
       string_agg(DISTINCT rv.reviewer, ', ') AS reviewers,
       bool_or(rv.reviewer IN (SELECT reviewer FROM wildcard)) AS wildcard_reviewer
FROM rv
JOIN nodes t ON t.value->>'name'=rv.target
            AND t.kind='identity_group' AND t.subkind='role'
WHERE coalesce(t.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND t.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
WITH roles AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT value->>'name' AS name
  FROM nodes WHERE kind='identity_group' AND subkind='role'
), rv AS (
  SELECT a.value->>'name' AS reviewer, r2.value->>'name' AS target
  FROM edges e
  JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=e.from_node AND a.kind='action' AND a.subkind='can_review'
  JOIN nodes r2 ON r2.id=e.to_node  AND r2.kind='identity_group' AND r2.subkind='role'
  WHERE e.kind='reviewer_of'
), wildcard AS (
  SELECT reviewer FROM rv
  GROUP BY reviewer
  HAVING count(DISTINCT target) >= (SELECT count(*) FROM roles)
)
SELECT rv.target AS target_role,
       string_agg(DISTINCT rv.reviewer, ', ') AS reviewers,
       bool_or(rv.reviewer IN (SELECT reviewer FROM wildcard)) AS wildcard_reviewer
FROM rv
JOIN nodes t ON t.value->>'name'=rv.target
            AND t.kind='identity_group' AND t.subkind='role'
WHERE coalesce(t.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND t.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Reviewers Per Role

panels.description:
Full inventory of every Teleport resource by type. Use labels to verify expected coverage or spot unlabelled resources.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT subkind AS kind, value->>'name' AS name, value->'labels' AS labels
FROM nodes WHERE kind='resource' ORDER BY subkind, name
```
panels.title: Resource Inventory

panels.description:
Roles ranked by real blast radius: does the role hold a wildcard resource selector, and how many distinct registered resources does it actually reach.

**Why this changed.** The previous query counted DISTINCT resource_group *node IDs*. Because Access Graph duplicates resource_group nodes (9 rows for 5 distinct selectors) that number was an artefact of the duplication, and by distinct selector name it was 1 for every role — so `role-kube-access` (wildcard over every Kubernetes cluster) tied `role-grafana-access` (two named apps). Ranking is now `has_wildcard` first, then distinct resources reached, which does discriminate: the wildcard-holding roles sort above `role-grafana-access` even though it reaches more resources by count.

**Caveat:** `resources_reachable` counts only resources *currently registered* with this cluster. A wildcard role reaching 1 resource today reaches every resource added tomorrow — which is exactly why `has_wildcard` is the primary sort key and not the count.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT r.value->>'name' AS role,
       bool_or(rg.value->>'name' = '{"*":"*"}')      AS has_wildcard,
       count(DISTINCT res.value->>'name')                AS resources_reachable,
       string_agg(DISTINCT a.subkind, ', ' ORDER BY a.subkind) AS resource_kinds
FROM nodes r
JOIN edges e1 ON e1.from_node=r.id AND e1.kind='access'
JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=e1.to_node   AND a.kind='action'
JOIN edges e2 ON e2.from_node=a.id AND e2.kind='access'
JOIN nodes rg ON rg.id=e2.to_node  AND rg.kind='resource_group'
LEFT JOIN edges e3 ON e3.from_node=rg.id AND e3.kind='access'
LEFT JOIN nodes res ON res.id=e3.to_node AND res.kind='resource'
WHERE r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
GROUP BY role
ORDER BY has_wildcard DESC, resources_reachable DESC, role
LIMIT 25
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT r.value->>'name' AS role,
       bool_or(rg.value->>'name' = '{"*":"*"}')      AS has_wildcard,
       count(DISTINCT res.value->>'name')                AS resources_reachable,
       string_agg(DISTINCT a.subkind, ', ' ORDER BY a.subkind) AS resource_kinds
FROM nodes r
JOIN edges e1 ON e1.from_node=r.id AND e1.kind='access'
JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=e1.to_node   AND a.kind='action'
JOIN edges e2 ON e2.from_node=a.id AND e2.kind='access'
JOIN nodes rg ON rg.id=e2.to_node  AND rg.kind='resource_group'
LEFT JOIN edges e3 ON e3.from_node=rg.id AND e3.kind='access'
LEFT JOIN nodes res ON res.id=e3.to_node AND res.kind='resource'
WHERE r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
GROUP BY role
ORDER BY has_wildcard DESC, resources_reachable DESC, role
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Blast Radius (Top 25 Roles)

panels.description:
Operator-authored roles granting **standing** access to the wildcard resource group `{"*":"*"}` — these bypass all label-based segmentation and have the highest effective blast radius.

Teleport preset/system and `bot-*` roles are excluded: `access`, `require-trusted-device`, `list-access-request-resources`, `requester` and `terraform-provider` hold wildcards by design and were 5 of the 8 roles previously listed, drowning the operator-authored ones.

The edge walk is now pinned to `kind='access'`. Without that, `requester_of` edges were followed too, which listed `role-base` here — but role-base can only *request* wildcard resources, it does not hold standing wildcard access. Requestable scope is shown in *Access Request Escalation Paths* instead.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT DISTINCT r.value->>'name' AS role, a.subkind AS resource_kind
FROM edges e1
JOIN nodes r  ON r.id=e1.from_node AND r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=e1.to_node   AND a.kind='action'
JOIN edges e2 ON e2.from_node=a.id AND e2.kind='access'
JOIN nodes rg ON rg.id=e2.to_node  AND rg.kind='resource_group'
WHERE rg.value->>'name' = '{"*":"*"}'
  AND coalesce(r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND r.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
ORDER BY role, resource_kind
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT DISTINCT r.value->>'name' AS role, a.subkind AS resource_kind
FROM edges e1
JOIN nodes r  ON r.id=e1.from_node AND r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
JOIN nodes a  ON a.id=e1.to_node   AND a.kind='action'
JOIN edges e2 ON e2.from_node=a.id AND e2.kind='access'
JOIN nodes rg ON rg.id=e2.to_node  AND rg.kind='resource_group'
WHERE rg.value->>'name' = '{"*":"*"}'
  AND coalesce(r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND r.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
ORDER BY role, resource_kind

panels.title: Wildcard-Access Roles

panels.description:
Distinct roles with at least one action requiring session MFA re-authentication (`require_mfa_type` set to anything other than `OFF`).

**Currently 0 — red is correct.** Verified live: every one of the 35 action nodes reads `require_mfa_type = 'OFF'`. Nothing on this cluster forces a second factor at session start. The table below lists every role so the OFF-all-the-way-down result is visible rather than filtered away.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT count(DISTINCT value->>'name') FROM nodes
WHERE kind='action'
  AND value->'properties'->'teleport'->>'require_mfa_type' NOT IN ('OFF')
```

targets.rawSql:

SELECT count(DISTINCT value->>'name') FROM nodes
WHERE kind='action'
  AND value->'properties'->'teleport'->>'require_mfa_type' NOT IN ('OFF')

panels.title: Roles Enforcing Session MFA

options.content:
### What this dashboard can and cannot tell you about MFA

**Can show — enrolment.** Per-user `weakest_mfa_device_kind` from Access Graph, split three ways above: has a device / explicitly has none / unknown (property absent, typically an SSO user).

**Can show — per-role enforcement.** `require_mfa_type` on each role's actions, in the table below. Currently `OFF` for all 35 action nodes: no role forces MFA re-authentication at session start.

**Cannot show — cluster policy.** The cluster-wide second-factor setting (`cluster_auth_preference.second_factor`, currently `otp` with no WebAuthn configured) is not available from **any** datasource wired into this Grafana. It lives in the Teleport backend, not in the Access Graph schema, and the `auth_preference.update` audit event records only `admin_actions_mfa_changed` — a boolean about admin-action MFA — not the second-factor value itself.

Surfacing cluster policy requires the planned **teleport-usage exporter** to read it from the Teleport API and expose it as a metric. Until then: enrolment and role enforcement here, cluster policy via `tctl get cluster_auth_preference`.

panels.description:
Per-role, per-action-kind session MFA enforcement (`require_mfa_type`) and trusted-device requirement, for every role that grants any action.

**The `<> 'OFF'` filter was removed on purpose.** With it, this panel returned exactly one row — `require-trusted-device`, reading `mfa = OFF` — which looked like a populated panel and hid the actual finding. Verified live: all 35 action nodes carry `require_mfa_type = 'OFF'` (5 more, the can_request/can_review actions, have no such property at all). **Zero roles on this cluster enforce session MFA.** Showing every role and letting the column read OFF all the way down is the honest presentation.

Cross-reference with *Wildcard-Access Roles*: the widest roles have no MFA re-auth requirement.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT DISTINCT
  value->>'name' AS role,
  subkind        AS action_kind,
  coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->>'require_mfa_type','(n/a)') AS require_mfa_type,
  coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->>'trusted_device','(none)')  AS trusted_device
FROM nodes
WHERE kind='action'
ORDER BY require_mfa_type DESC, role, action_kind
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT DISTINCT
  value->>'name' AS role,
  subkind        AS action_kind,
  coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->>'require_mfa_type','(n/a)') AS require_mfa_type,
  coalesce(value->'properties'->'teleport'->>'trusted_device','(none)')  AS trusted_device
FROM nodes
WHERE kind='action'
ORDER BY require_mfa_type DESC, role, action_kind

panels.title: Per-Role Session MFA Enforcement

panels.description:
Operator-authored roles for which the Access Graph shows **no** member_of, impersonator_of or requester_of edge — i.e. no grant path the graph can see.

**Read this as a review prompt, not a delete list.** The Access Graph does not model login-rule / SSO role grants: a role handed to an SSO user by a login rule produces no graph edge at all. Verified on this cluster — `jturner@b1tsized.tech` has zero member_of edges, yet audit `access_request.create` events record their standing `user_roles` as `["role-base","role-grafana-access","role-kube-access-auto-approved"]`. All three roles currently listed here are exactly those, so all three are false positives. A listed role may well be live; confirm against login rules and the audit log before removing anything.

Teleport preset/system and generated `bot-*` roles are excluded — they are shipped unused by design and previously made up 14 of the 17 reported "dead" roles.

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT DISTINCT r.value->>'name' AS role,
       r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->>'description' AS description
FROM nodes r
WHERE r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
  AND coalesce(r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND r.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM nodes r2
    JOIN edges e ON e.to_node = r2.id
    WHERE r2.kind='identity_group' AND r2.subkind='role'
      AND r2.value->>'name' = r.value->>'name'
      AND e.kind IN ('member_of','impersonator_of','requester_of')
  )
ORDER BY role
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT DISTINCT r.value->>'name' AS role,
       r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->>'description' AS description
FROM nodes r
WHERE r.kind='identity_group' AND r.subkind='role'
  AND coalesce(r.value->'properties'->'teleport'->'labels'->>'teleport.internal/resource-type','') NOT IN ('preset','system')
  AND r.value->>'name' NOT LIKE 'bot-%'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM nodes r2
    JOIN edges e ON e.to_node = r2.id
    WHERE r2.kind='identity_group' AND r2.subkind='role'
      AND r2.value->>'name' = r.value->>'name'
      AND e.kind IN ('member_of','impersonator_of','requester_of')
  )
ORDER BY role

panels.description:
All security alerts from Access Graph, most recent first. `severity` and `status` are now surfaced as the leading, colour-coded columns — this cluster's 22 alerts are all `severity=high` / `status=in_progress`, and `in_progress` (not `OPEN`) is the only not-yet-closed status this schema emits.

`title` and `affected_entity` are lifted out of the `data` blob so a row is readable without expanding JSON; the full structured finding is still in the `data` column.

**Alerts are triaged and closed inside Teleport (Identity Security -> Security Alerts), not in Grafana.**

**SQL:**
```sql
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT
  severity,
  status,
  kind,
  data->'affected_entity'->>'name' AS affected_entity,
  data->>'title'                   AS title,
  data->>'created_at'              AS created_at,
  data
FROM security_alerts
ORDER BY (data->>'created_at') DESC
LIMIT 50
```

targets.rawSql:
SET search_path TO ${tenant};
SELECT
  severity,
  status,
  kind,
  data->'affected_entity'->>'name' AS affected_entity,
  data->>'title'                   AS title,
  data->>'created_at'              AS created_at,
  data
FROM security_alerts
ORDER BY (data->>'created_at') DESC
LIMIT 50
